newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: James Baker begins Western Sahara mission April 22.
newsitem.headline: James Baker begins Western Sahara mission April 22.

text.p: Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, named last month as the U.N. secretary-general's personal envoy for the Western Sahara problem, will begin a visit to the region April 22, a U.N. spokesman said on Friday.
Western Sahara is disputed between Morocco, which controls most of the former Spanish colony, and the Algerian-backed Polisario independence movement.

A U.N. settlement plan calls for a referendum on the future of the territory but it has been repeatedly postponed since January 1992 because of differences between the two sides over who should be eligible to vote.
Baker will visit Rabat, the Moroccan capital; Tindouf, the Polisario base on the Algerian side of the border; Algiers; and Nouakchott, the capital of Mauritania.

"Mr Baker will make a fresh assessment of the situation and will examine, together with the parties and the neighbouring countries, obstacles blocking the implementation of the settlement plan for Western Sahara. He will report to the secretary-general on his findings," the U.N. spokesman said.
